> Only live slice/finding tracker. Current work: [ROADMAP](ROADMAP.md); current rules: [AGENTS](../AGENTS.md).

**This is the only live slice/subslice tracker.** Updated 2026-09-14 with the DIAG programme.
Current focus is the single pointer in [context](../context.md); this table alone owns live state.
The last shipped execution milestone is [CEIR-35](sessions/2026-09-11-ceir-35z-band-close.md).
Agent entry: [START_HERE](../START_HERE.md). Broad architecture/gaps:
[whole-system review](research/2026-09-12-cerid-whole-system-review.md); every G01–G30 finding has owners in this table.

## Purpose

Build the fully authorable, performant, cross-API renderer; the complete Cerid-owned UI; and **CR-D007**, the game
and engineering application editor. Algorithms, shaders, pipelines, frame graphs and behaviour are editable assets:
CHIR authors high-level behaviour, CEIR executes, CKIR expresses device kernels. The editor is a consumer of public
modules. Standalone games, engineering apps, the notebook and later DAWs use those same modules.

## Confirmed order and decisions

Recorded in [ADR-0129](decisions/0129-renderer-ui-editor-delivery-order.md).

**2026-09-14 user addition:** immediately after REPO.DEV, complete the **DIAG** runtime diagnostic foundation,
then the retained repository close and renderer sequence below. [ADR-0133](decisions/0133-runtime-diagnostics-and-instrumentation.md)
and the [DIAG contract](design/runtime-diagnostics.md) define all children; the [research](research/2026-09-14-diagnostics-and-instrumentation.md)
maps DG01–DG18 source findings. Existing CI/review gates remain. MAC.DIAG/WEB.DIAG qualify later-platform integration;
the early foundation must not depend on a future editor or claim universal bug detection.

1. Complete the **entire retained renderer feature library**, including virtual geometry, hybrid GI, neural rendering
   dependencies and OFF-1…9 production offline rendering. This is the user's explicit choice on 2026-09-12.
2. Build full `crd-ui` and CR-D007. Bootstrap the shell at I2D-4, then build the remaining widgets within it.
3. Finish hesap GPU and the MATLAB-like notebook, as a CR-D007 workspace **and** a thin standalone host.
4. Resume media, audio/plugins, later applications and preserved engine/domain work. Windows/Linux qualify first;
   macOS and web follow explicitly. Physics/geometry and unrelated code are untouched by this documentation audit.

The expanded AI programme qualifies **training and inference together**, including scoped full training, fine-tuning,
distillation and specialized game/product agents. Neural-renderer dependencies qualify before UI. Collaboration uses
an authoritative project host with local/offline recovery; multiplayer has a separate authoritative simulation contract.
[ADR-0130](decisions/0130-system-qualification-and-agent-driven-products.md) distinguishes confirmed product directions
from proposed mechanism choices. Broader modeling, DAW, CAD/CAM/EDA, embedded, digital-twin and hardware work remains
in the same sequence with explicit qualification children; no retained ID was removed.

Renderer `.runtime` rows finish the full runtime/asset work before UI. `.authoring` children then prove those same
features in CR-D007; the original family ID closes only afterward. This preserves the visual-authoring requirement
without pretending an editor exists before UI. Media codec IDs remain MED-1…12; MED-GPU-* identifies the separate
architecture contracts that formerly reused the same numbers.

**Still to review before implementation:** RAH-0's refreshed no-loss design and ADR-0107's full proposal. The language,
service and qualification recommendations are concrete in the execution contract. The audit request authorizes
documentation changes, not an invented ADR acceptance. No unavailable advisor sign-off is claimed. The old CEIR loop
grant ended with CEIR-35; this table does not silently reinstate it.

## How to use this document

Read [context](../context.md) for the current pointer, then this table. Open only the row's detail and ADR for work.
The [execution contract](design/renderer-ui-execution-contract.md) defines ownership, quality, publishing and UI gates.
The [inherited catalogue](design/rendering-ui-contracts.md) contains the complete feature lists; a short table cell
does not reduce them. The [audit](research/2026-09-12-system-audit.md) contains findings, evidence and module inventory.
[Systems](systems/README.md) maps the code; [decisions](decisions/README.md) records architecture.

**States:** Done = complete contract with evidence and sequential acceptance; In progress = the sole current row;
Blocked = named unmet non-CI gate; Needs CI = available local work finished, published CI output still required;
Recorded = dated evidence/documentation, not a new test run; Review = unresolved census/decision;
Open = unimplemented/unqualified contract; Partial = retained work/evidence awaiting full sequential acceptance.
There is no Later state (user decision 2026-10-27): every row is planned in its exact order, grouped with its
family; the [delivery plan](design/delivery-plan.md) explains the order. Source plans and archives never carry live status. Capability maturity is a separate
machine-derived fact in [the registry](capabilities/gpu-platform-capabilities.toml), not inferred from these states.

Query `python scripts/check-master-plan.py --slice RAH-1`, `--find A24`, or `--next` for a small view of this same table.
Finding IDs link directly to evidence; the linked owner rows carry their live state. No second bug backlog is allowed.

## Strict sequential execution

**Latest user direction, 2026-09-12:** start at the earliest unfinished work unless explicitly directed to a future
slice. Leave no gaps. If evidence needs CI output, say so and continue available work. This supersedes the earlier
same-day rule that stopped all advancement while CI waited; other scope, hardware and renderer review gates remain.

1. Walk the Order column. Done and historical Recorded rows require no implementation; Needs CI rows retain an
   external verification gate. The first remaining row is the default work position, including Open, Partial, Review
   and Blocked. Context points there; only that row may be In progress. Finish all available work in that row first.
2. **Needs CI is not Done.** Use it only when all presently available local work is finished and published CI output
   is the remaining evidence. Link the actual run and dated local proof in the row. Say "needs CI output" and continue
   the next available work; never drop its requirements, weaken an oracle or claim an unobserved pass. Inspect changed
   CI results first on re-entry: a real failure returns to its owning row and takes priority in table order.
3. An explicit user request to work on a future slice overrides default scheduling, not its prerequisites/quality.
   Record the exact user direction in a session and link it in that row as `[User direction](sessions/<record>.md)`
   with `<!-- user-order: sessions/<record>.md -->`. This marker may be added only for a real explicit instruction,
   never inferred from a quality goal, old grant or agent-written plan. Return to earliest work after that assignment.
4. All full contracts, children, tests, publication/provider evidence and documentation remain required for Done.
   A pending prerequisite is not waived by continued work. Parents close only when every child and inherited gate
   closes. Hardware/design/scope blockers remain binding unless the user explicitly changes their contract.
5. Add a proven missing prerequisite before its owning unfinished row, with references and rationale. Never move
   unrelated work forward, reorder the table to conceal a gap or reclassify unfinished implementation as Recorded.
   New findings keep owning rows and exact evidence; CI waits and parked work are visible in this same table.
6. Previously parked later work remains Partial with its implementation/evidence intact. At its turn audit the full
   contract; reuse valid proof and run missing or newly justified checks. The validator enforces the default order,
   one active position, referenced user overrides and explicitly retained CI waits. No second status queue is allowed.

The [initial order correction](sessions/2026-09-12-strict-slice-order.md) preserves earlier evidence; the
[CI continuation amendment](sessions/2026-09-12-ci-continuation-and-dx12-workloads.md) records the latest direction.
New child IDs are proposed execution decomposition, clearly distinct from original source IDs. Add every additional
child here before implementing it; never create another tracker. A large row starts with a detailed reuse/design/
test note linked from its contract cell. Parent completion requires all children and inherited requirements.

| 052 | <a id="slice-repo.dev.6"></a>**REPO.DEV.6** | Done | One registry (`cmake/pins.json`) names every external input with version, commit-addressed source, SHA-256 and license: the nine CPM packages acquire as verified archives (`crd_add_pinned_package`, `CRD_INPUT_ARCHIVES` for verified offline copies), the CPM bootstrap, Vulkan SDK, Vulkan headers, SPIRV-Reflect, WARP and actionlint acquire through helpers that download to a partial file and verify before the final name exists, the imgui Vulkan patch applies to a build-owned copy from a versioned spec (the shared cache stays pristine, a drifted anchor fails the configure), every workflow action is a commit with its tag, every runner an explicit image, every checkout `persist-credentials: false`; `check-pins.py` guards the registry at configure, in preflight and in the tooling tests. Local proof: the full `win-debug` graph unchanged except the patched path, Linux reconfigured, four consumers on one source cache with the tree hash identical after the third and the fourth; hosted lanes on the next push. **Hosted (2026-10-06 audit):** not yet shown. Run 37311671924 verified the Vulkan headers, the validation layer and sccache on download, but every lane restored its CPM archive cache (and Windows its Vulkan SDK cache) through the restore-key fallback, as did the first complete run; cold acquisition of every archive, the Vulkan SDK and WARP through the verifying helpers has never run hosted. Needs one cache-cold hosted run. **Cold lanes landed (2026-10-06, user decision: a standing step, option 2):** the complete-tier `win-debug-scalar` and `linux-gcc-debug-scalar` skip every archive cache (`CRD_COLD_PRESETS`); `check-cold-acquisition.py` fails unless the CPM cache starts empty and every package the configure added is pinned and acquired (the Windows lane also installs the Vulkan SDK and the pinned WARP); proven by a real cold configure on the WSL reference host and its tooling test. The next complete-tier run is the hosted proof. **Hosted (2026-10-06, complete run 37395083192):** both cold lanes started from an empty cache. Each acquired all seven packages any configuration selects (Catch2, glfw, zstd, stb, cgltf, MikkTSpace, imgui), verified each against its pinned SHA-256, and passed its whole test lane. The Windows lane also installed the Vulkan SDK 1.4.341.1 and WARP 1.0.20 cold through their verifying helpers. Not yet shown: the two gated pins (Eigen and OpenBLAS, `CRD_BUILD_HESAP_VS_REFERENCE`, which no hosted preset builds), named but never acquired. Rather than leave them unproven, both cold lanes now also download and verify every unselected pin's archive (`check-cold-acquisition.py --fetch-unselected`, through `pins.download`). Partial construction: owning arenas whose parent refuses now reach their own fatal instead of building on null (six specimen modes), the growable pool refuses a page non-fatally, and `construct`/`construct_array` handle refusal, count overflow and throwing constructors. Clean controls pass on every route; the 2,000-instruction control reports the write out of the log. 34 mocked verdict tests (`crd-diag-reverse-debug-recipes`, a repository CI step on both runners); CI installs and records `gdb`; teeth shown (the off-by-one repaired, any reverse stop taken as the writer, truncation not distinguished, any cdb stop taken as the writer). **Seed, choice and input minimization landed locally** (2026-10-10, committed, not pushed): `crd/core/minimize.hpp` holds the DIAG.4b greedy remover promoted (`minimize_sequence`, 1-minimal), `bisect_toward` and `minimize_toward_zero`, under an all-K-runs oracle (a candidate that fails on some runs only is a race, counted `flaky` and never kept; a candidate is never judged on fewer than K runs; a run budget stops with a result that still reproduces, not claimed minimal; an input that does not reproduce is left as given). Choices: the schedule-script minimization runs through it (K = 3) and still yields `{test.reacquired, fp.finalizing}` (local only: `crd-jobs-schedcheck-tests` is in no hosted job). Seed and hits: `minimize_fault_plan` (crd-perf) narrows each rule's range by bisection, pins the plan to the hits it fires on (seed 0, every rule always firing) and removes single hits or rules to a 1-minimal plan; shown on synthetic programs (every-allocation plan to its one needed hit, a seeded four-rule plan to its two needed hits on two sites), on a real injector through a `FaultAllocator`, and on the real cooker (a 40% read plan whose cook recovered from two faults shrinks to the one `.meta` read that fails it, each kept hit checked needed). | 089 | <a id="slice-diag.10a"></a>**DIAG.10a** | Done | Stateful production-path fuzzing for allocators, diagnostics, current commands/reload and IR differentials; DG16. **Allocator operation sequences landed locally** (2026-10-10, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-10-diag-10a-allocator-fuzzing.md)): `crd-fuzz-memory-allocators` (`tests/foundation/memory/fuzz`, harness and corpus replay CTest on every lane, libFuzzer on `linux-clang-fuzz`) drives TLSF, pool, linear, stack, the growable TLSF, pool and linear, the offset allocator, the epoch ring, the `DiagnosticAllocator` over TLSF and the `SlotMap` with decoded operation streams against an independent model (no overlap, alignment, ownership, intact payloads, exact capacity models, `validate_structure()`, statistics back to zero, offset coalescing, parent leak check, identical outcome trace on a second run); only contract-valid operations reach raw allocators, malformed sizes and alignments are refused, and the checked layers take double, interior, foreign and evicted frees, redzone overruns, writes into quarantine and stale, double-erased and forged handles. Seven defects found and fixed, each kept as a corpus input (five as written seeds, two as adopted libFuzzer inputs): TLSF `try_allocate` asserted on a non-power-of-two alignment; TLSF in-place reallocation never adjusted `bytes_in_use`; the linear, stack and growable linear allocators drove `bytes_in_use` past zero by alignment padding; the `DiagnosticAllocator` passed interior pointers and evicted double frees to its backing heap and named the discarded block in its saturation report; a TLSF pool whose capacity is not a multiple of 16 put its end sentinel at a misaligned address (UBSan, found by libFuzzer); `OffsetAllocator::reset()` kept node neighbour links, so the next whole-span free coalesced with regions that no longer existed (found by libFuzzer). Every `crd_fuzz_target()` now has a `fuzz.py` entry, enforced by `test-repository-tools.py` (the bundle target had none); the replay driver is headless, so an engine assertion fails a replay instead of hanging it on a dialog. Four bounded libFuzzer rounds (4 workers); the last ran 587 s, 256,345 executions, no artifact; two reports were the harness's own (an offset span no bin represents cannot be handed out whole by design; an evicted pointer is ambiguous while a saturation passthrough block is live) and the harness was corrected. Teeth: twelve engine breaks and one registry break each fail their seed or test. Corpus 23 inputs (17 written, 6 adopted). **The crd-perf evidence readers landed locally** (2026-10-10, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-10-diag-10a-evidence-readers.md)): three more targets in `tests/foundation/perf/fuzz` with corpora under `corpus/<reader>/` (the bundle corpus moved to `corpus/bundle/`), each in `fuzz.py`: `crd-fuzz-perf-flight` (`decode_flight_record`; an accepted record must be one a `FlightRecorder` can write, restated independently in the harness, and re-encode to its own bytes), `crd-fuzz-perf-assets` (the flight-policy and fault-plan assets and the fault-plan text over crd-toml; a refusal leaves the output untouched, an accepted policy or plan round-trips through its canonical form) and `crd-fuzz-perf-capture` (`validate_capture_buffer` and `CaptureView` against a reference CPROF layout the harness computes from the header). Seed functions check every seed's verdict as they write it (`VerdictSink`). Findings fixed: the flight-record decoder accepted self-contradicting records (an unarmed trigger, suppressed kinds without a count, an end reason the post window contradicts, a ringless capture with events, gaps across the trigger, a clip flag on a short message, Info under Basic, an unavailable replay without a reason); the CPROF reader trusted every offset behind its section sizes (a name-blob size that wraps the section sum, unchecked sample arrays, blob slots, offsets and terminators, unterminated names, unknown counter kinds and types, counts past the profiler's tables and a frame record's arrays, an unaligned buffer); crd-toml had no nesting bound (a 20,000-deep array overflowed the stack) and clamped silently (an integer past the 64-bit range read as `INT64_MAX`, a float overflow as infinity, a number token past 63 characters cut short), now refused past 64 levels and out of range; libFuzzer found the Perfetto export's span `end - begin` overflowing `i64` (UBSan), now computed without overflow (adopted input `6ea98773...`). No on-disk layout or record version changed. Single-process libFuzzer rounds: flight 24.7 M executions, assets 0.9 M, capture 2.9 M after the fix, all clean; teeth: 25 deliberate breaks, each failing its seed or case. Open: under four concurrent processes, two perf targets (the unchanged bundle target too) showed input-independent register and stack corruption that no artifact reproduces; single-process runs are clean; the cause is not established (recorded in the session). **Run records landed locally** (2026-10-10, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-10-diag-10a-run-records.md)): `crd-fuzz-ceir-record` (`tests/execution/ceir-cook/fuzz`, in `fuzz.py`; crd-ceir-cook's module now owns the harness directory) decodes each input as given and again with its header's payload size and checksum recomputed, so mutated payloads reach the payload reader; an accepted record must be one `replay.record`, `record_host_run` or the device recorder can write (restated in the harness), re-encode to its own bytes, name exactly the missing inputs its states name and show no divergence from a trace that repeats it, and the decoder may allocate at most eight times the input plus 64 KiB. Findings fixed in `decode_record`: it reserved arrays from counts before checking the bytes left (a record under 500 bytes reserved 3 MB of events, 1.5 MB of reads or 16 MB of device words), and it accepted records no recorder writes: an input state its need contradicts, program, build or arguments not needed-and-recorded, external results recorded, a schedule recorded off the host executor or missing on a host record, a device tolerance recorded off the device executor or missing on a device record, a seam input recorded when only possibly needed or past the 65,536-read bound, a kept read of an input said not needed, a cancelled run, a kernel whose text does not hash to its recorded hash, device kernels or buffers in a plan or host record; `replay.prepare` presented such claims as available inputs. Such record files are now refused at `replay.run` and `replay.prepare` as not decoding; the DIAG.9b external-results cases were split accordingly (the file route refused as malformed, `record_missing_inputs` asserted on the same claims in memory, honest needed-and-missing records still refused as missing), the device case for edited kernel text checks the decoder and the in-memory replay, two ceir-host fixtures that turned a host record into a plan record now store the schedule as the plan recorder does, and a new check covers the unheld-stream rule the corpus cannot reach (a stream past 65,536 reads exceeds the 64 KiB input bound). No layout or schema changed. Corpus 57 seeds (8 honest records, 30 one-way forgeries, 19 structural); 14 teeth each fail the corpus replay or the new check. **Command decoding landed locally** (2026-10-10, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-10-diag-10a-command-decoding.md)): `crd-fuzz-ceridc-diag` (`tests/tools/ceridc/fuzz`, in `fuzz.py`; the ceridc module owns the harness directory) feeds ceridc's stdio MCP transport line by line (the owned JSON parser, `mcp_handle`, the diag tool's decoding, `DiagCommandService::execute` with every command ceridc binds and the sandbox's flight and fault commands, under a host line's grant and an optional file root that does not exist; lines that could reach ceridc's file verbs are not fed), plus native requests of raw bytes. Oracles: an independent iterative RFC 8259 and UTF-8 validator agreeing with the parser within its limits, JSON-RPC replies (one line of valid UTF-8, -32700, -32600 with a null id, no reply to a notification, the id echoed exactly), the diag tool's decoding restated with its report equal byte for byte to the native answer for the page it names, the service's refusal order restated (no handler runs on a refusal; a command's check answers only bad-argument or unavailable), document fields equal to the typed result, page bounds, a walk to the end of every snapshot with repeatable cursors, and no allocation left live. Findings fixed: the JSON parser accepted numbers outside the grammar (`+1`, `01`, `.5`, `1.`), read a token past 63 characters as its first 63, turned an overflow into infinity and accepted ill-formed UTF-8 (now the RFC grammar read whole by `std::from_chars`, out of range and ill-formed UTF-8 refused; `crd/core/utf8.hpp`); `as_i64` cast doubles past the i64 range (undefined; now the default); the MCP transport answered string ids as 0 and rounded or truncated others, silently dropped a batch array or bare value, compared method and tool names as C strings cut at a NUL, cut string arguments past 511 bytes or at a NUL to another path, read a non-boolean `dry_run` as false (a `"true"` string wrote the file) and cast frame counts and translations from any double (ids now echo exactly or the request is -32600; arguments are used as sent or the call is -32602); crd-perf's and crd-asset-io's JSON writers passed ill-formed UTF-8 through and the service cut its command echo inside a sequence (now `\ufffd` and a boundary clip), so a document is valid UTF-8 whatever bytes a request or evidence held; libFuzzer found a refusal's typed cursor left at 0 while its document named the request's (now every typed field matches). Corpus 52 seeds; 20 teeth each fail the corpus replay or a unit case; three single-process libFuzzer rounds of 600 s (the last 123,357 executions, no artifact). The commands' own file readers open files outside crd-core's I/O fault seam, so which paths they open is not observed (the target's root does not exist). **Resource reload landed locally** (2026-10-10, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-10-diag-10a-resource-reload.md)): `crd-fuzz-resources-reload` (`tests/assets/resources/fuzz`, in `fuzz.py`; the resources module owns the harness directory) writes each pack an input names to a per-process temp file and drives the real `ResourceManager`: raw pack bytes (read by `crdr_read`, then mounted, loaded, reloaded, evicted, loaded again, unmounted) or a script over two packs (built through `CrdrWriter` and overridden with lying ranges, duplicated ids, torn tails, compressed or dropped chunks; raw bytes; in-place corruption; mount, unmount, `load_sync`, release, `reload_mount_now`, drain to a zero budget, pin). Oracles: a restated CRDR layout and pack rule set (zstd decoding the compressed chunks), an allocation bound on `crdr_read`, and a model of the manager compared after every operation with `find_entry`, `entry_count`, `mount_count`, `current_memory_use` and every held handle; a payload reaches only its own type's loader; every byte is returned. Findings fixed: `crdr_read` reserved what compressed chunks claimed before decoding them (a 96-byte file reserved 1 TiB; two claims whose sum wraps reserved 16 bytes and decoded 32 into them) and kept a zero-filled tail when a frame decoded short (claims now bounded by `crdr_max_decompressed_size` and decoded exactly); `do_reload_mount` copied a torn pack's offsets into the live table before any range check and checked reloaded ranges with a sum that wraps, reloaded an id a newer mount served from the older pack, swapped a retyped entry's payload into a block of the old type (freed by the wrong loader), ignored added ids, kept dropped ids at stale offsets, swapped a duplicated id twice and never re-accounted the resident size; `unmount` erased ids an older mount still provided, contrary to its header; a re-issue after eviction crossed types; a manifest naming one id twice mounted. A pack is now taken whole or not at all by mount and both reload paths (unreadable, unparsable, torn or a duplicated id refuses it), the live table serves each id from the newest mount naming it, and an id keeps its type across reload and re-issue (`resource_manager.hpp`). The replay driver ends on a Debug CRT report instead of a modal dialog. Corpus 34 seeds; 12 teeth each fail the corpus replay; two single-process libFuzzer rounds of 600 s (152,294 and 106,198 executions) found nothing further. **The compiled and reference CEIR comparison landed locally** (2026-10-10, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-10-diag-10a-ceir-differential.md)): `crd-fuzz-ceir-differential` (`tests/execution/ceir/fuzz`, in `fuzz.py`) decodes every input to a generated program inside the cook's module-validity set (arith, core control flow, the three cell kinds, calls with recursion, async and task tokens, data-parallel bodies, the input ops; up to four functions, a step budget of 64 to 131,072, a scripted host input or none) and runs it through the reference interpreter and the compiled plan, which must agree on the error class, values, every cell, every map output and the op an error blames (stable id); only the documented compile refusal (a stateful or input-reading parallel body) is accepted, and the plan run twice, a fresh reference session and the printed and serialized twins must give the same outcome. Findings fixed in both tiers: the reference charged every terminator a step, so the tiers ran out of steps at different ops (a step is now a dispatched non-terminator op, a loop iteration, a parallel-range index or a fold step; `plan::run` takes `max_steps`); unbounded recursion overflowed the native stack (on win-asan near 190 nesting levels, 180 through a `map_reduce` body), now `NestingTooDeep` at `exec::kMaxNesting` = 64 in both tiers, blamed on the same op, a parallel body's sub-interpreter starting at its parent's level (the value appended to both error enums; `kLastExecError`/`kLastRunError` bound the run-record decoder); a parallel range's `hi - lo` and indices overflowed i64 (a full-i64 range by 2^62 came out empty), the reference reserved a map slot per index before running any body (16 GiB for a 2^31-index range) and an instruction-free body was unbounded (each index and fold step is now a step, counted in unsigned arithmetic by `exec::parallel_range_count`); a `for` step past INT64_MAX overflowed `iv += step`; the compiled `parallel_for`/`map_reduce` re-entered from its own body mixed the inner activation's entries into the outer map; libFuzzer found that the reference lost the map of a parallel op inside a parallel body (its sub-interpreter was discarded; the parent now adopts it) that the plan's per-body token scope moved the whole run-wide token store (quadratic; now a base index), and that both tiers gave each parallel body a fresh copy of the budget, so a body re-entering the program ran for minutes (a parallel body's steps are now the run's). Eight `[diag10a]` cases in crd-ceir-tests pin the agreed answers. Corpus 35 (32 seeds, 3 adopted inputs; the slowest replays in about 2 s under ASan); 15 teeth each fail the corpus replay, a unit case or libFuzzer's 10 s limit (the two overflow teeth only through the unit cases on MSVC, and as UBSan reports on `linux-clang-fuzz`). **The host provider's parallel range landed locally** (2026-10-11, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-11-diag-10a-host-parallel-range.md)): the crd-jobs provider counts and indexes a range with `exec::parallel_range_count`/`parallel_range_index` (it computed `hi - lo` in i64 and cut the count to 32 bits: `[INT64_MIN, INT64_MAX)` by 2^62 came out empty, 2^32 + 3 indices ran as 3, 2^33 as none); its budget rule is now stated and tested: what the submitting thread runs spends the run's budget as in the reference (one step per index, spent with the new `Interpreter::spend_fuel(steps)` before any per-index slot is sized, so a range past the budget is FuelExhausted on the parallel op with nothing allocated, and the map_reduce fold, which ran on one uncharged `sub_fuel` budget), while each body a pool worker runs keeps its per-item `sub_fuel`; a range index's body, a fold step and a pooled launch body start at the level of the op that runs them (`Interpreter::set_nesting`, the level carried with the job), so they stop at `kMaxNesting` on the op the reference blames (each started at level 0); worker bodies run on Medium fibers, because on win-asan a body past about 35 levels faulted on its 64 KiB Small fiber's guard page and ended the process with no report (34 levels fitted, 36 did not); each body's scratch starts with a 64 KiB chunk instead of the 256 MiB default (256 indices took 16.8 s on win-debug, now 0.27 s). Six `[ceir][host][diag10a]` cases in `crd-ceir-host-tests` compare the provider with the reference on the same module (nesting parity for the three body kinds, every level usable on a worker, the whole-line range, the budget refusal with no allocation, the fold budget, the submitting thread's remaining budget equal to the reference's); eight teeth each fail them (the Small-fiber tooth crashes win-asan; it passes on win-debug, which fits 62 levels in 64 KiB). The provider is not in a fuzz target: per-item budgets, the NoSemantics refusal of a parallel op inside a body and launch errors raised at await make its agreement with the sequential tiers a filtered oracle. **The virtual-memory and streaming allocators landed locally** (2026-10-11, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-11-diag-10a-vm-streaming-allocators.md)): two more kinds of `crd-fuzz-memory-allocators` (appended, so every committed input keeps its kind), each input reserving at most 16 MiB and releasing it with the allocator. The `VirtualMemoryAllocator` is held to an exact model of its bump offset and committed high-water mark (whole commit blocks capped at the reservation, purge to the page holding the live top, recommitted bytes reading zero, the tail poisoned under ASan, in-place reallocation only of the top block); the `StreamingAllocator` runs under an input-scripted residency policy (shed the category, any category, one block, nothing, or claim bytes never freed) with every category's charge tracked exactly, the budget held on every success, the retry bound (17 consultations) and no consultation for a request nothing can serve. Findings fixed: the arena's `try_allocate` asserted on a non-power-of-two alignment; a commit block that is a page multiple but not a power of two was rounded with the power-of-two mask, and one too large for any page multiple wrapped to one page; a reallocate of the top block asking for a stricter alignment returned it in place, misaligned; a request no resident heap can serve (non-power-of-two alignment, larger than the reservation, aligned past any chunk) reached the eviction loop, so the policy shed resident data for it; `GrowableTlsfAllocator::try_allocate` took a new chunk from its parent for a non-power-of-two alignment and then refused it (a chunk left behind per request, committed for good under a virtual-memory parent); the streaming budget checked the request but charged the heap's block, so rounding carried a category past its budget (it now holds the charge, sheds for a block rounded past the remaining budget and refuses, without consulting the policy, a block larger than the whole budget). One `[memory][streaming][diag10a]` case in `crd-memory-tests` pins the last refusal. Corpus 37 (31 written, 6 adopted); 11 teeth each fail a seed or the case (one, the arena's commit left unpoisoned, on win-asan). **The unknown-origin CEIR and CKIR artifacts reinvestigated locally** (2026-10-11, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-11-diag-10a-unknown-origin-artifacts.md)): the four loader targets gained cross-format oracles (an accepted CEIR text module must serialize, deserialize and print back to the same text; an accepted CEIR blob must print to text the parser accepts and prints identically; an accepted CKIR blob must write `.ckir` text that reads back to the same blob), the contracts `binary.hpp` and `ckir_asset.hpp` already state. On that harness the six artifacts adopted by REPO.DEV.11 (`553e7ecf`, `d85628dd`, `183a3e2e`, `e18eb14e`, `34ce93c0`, `c7c59902`) each replay clean alone, 10,000 times in one process under ASan and UBSan with stack-use-after-return and strict string checks, and under valgrind memcheck on linux-gcc-debug; none reproduces its round-four symptom, so they stay labelled unknown. The new oracles found real defects, each fixed with corpus inputs: the CEIR binary loader accepted names the text form cannot express (an op name `tes).sink`, which `183a3e2e` carries, a trait `2rd`, any struct, enum, param, trait, field, case, symbolic-dim, type-class or attr-class name outside `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*`, an empty symbol ref) and a type attribute naming no type, whose printing asserted in `type_of`; the CEIR text reader refused the zero-member `!tuple<>` and `!variant<>` the type model, the factories and the printer allow; the CKIR blob loader accepted out-of-range op, dtype, kind, tier, statement, scope, stage, depth and interpolation bytes (which index past the text writer's name tables), a rank past 8, dims past the rank and stray stage-output slots, and the `.ckir` reader refused the INT64_MIN its writer emits. Ten CEIR and seven CKIR written seeds, each checked refused as it is written, four adopted libFuzzer findings and two adopted inputs that crashed only inside a libFuzzer process (see below); one `[diag10a]` case in `crd-ceir-tests`; twelve teeth each fail a corpus or the case. The corruption of unknown origin recurred twice in that batch in single libFuzzer processes (a UBSan object-size report on `Array<u8>`'s container annotation in `crd-fuzz-ceir-text`, an ASan SEGV writing address 4 at the end of `asan_annotate_live_range` in `crd-fuzz-ckir-binary`) and once in a 10,000-repetition replay (a container overflow on the byte `push_back` had just annotated); each input replays clean (30,000 and 328,000 further repetitions), a known-answer CPU probe was clean (about 150,000 passes in WSL, 64,000 on Windows) and Windows logged `cl.exe` access violations at ten different offsets in 30 days. **The container-overflow control ran locally** (2026-10-11, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-11-diag-10a-container-overflow-control.md)): with `detect_container_overflow=0` (shown to disable the annotation in this runtime) libFuzzer processes paired by seed, run count and moment faulted 7 times in 12 against 8 in 12 with the default (about one event per 1.5 M and 1.0 M executions), one of them inside `asan_annotate_live_range` itself, so the annotation path is where the corruption is noticed, not where it is made. Two bounded follow-up slots showed that neither libFuzzer, the sanitizers nor the input is needed: the replay driver faulted 130 times in about 2.31 M executions, an unsanitized linux-gcc-debug loop faulted twice in about 4.68 M (once as a wrong result on an input it handled correctly 5,922 other times), every artifact replays clean and one equals a committed seed; `MallocAllocator::try_allocate` asserted `is_pow2` on the constant 8 its caller loads just before the call. | 091 | <a id="slice-diag.10c"></a>**DIAG.10c** | Done | Numerical/type/unit/time-domain and resource-pressure sanity probes plus lifecycle/soak oracles; DG16. **Numerical-mode expectation and the jobs boundary landed locally** (2026-10-11, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-11-diag-10c-numerical-mode.md)): the declared mode is the thread-start mode (MXCSR `0x1F80`: all exceptions masked, round to nearest even, no FTZ/DAZ; x87 control word `0x027F` on Windows, `0x037F` on Linux), only control bits are compared, and `crd/core/fp_environment.hpp` reads, writes, scopes and compares it field by field (an unread field is `Unread`, never a match; the x87 word is read where GNU inline assembly exists). At the crd-jobs boundary every job starts in the declared mode whatever its thread's mode, keeps a mode it sets across its waits and migrations, and loses it when it ends. Defect found and fixed: the Linux fiber switch saved neither MXCSR nor the x87 control word (its comment called them caller-saved; the psABI makes their control bits callee-saved), so a job's flush-to-zero or rounding mode reached the worker's scheduler stack and every later job, and a waiting job resumed in another job's mode; four `[diag10c]` cases in crd-jobs-tests all failed on the old switch on linux-gcc-debug and pass with `fiber_switch_lin64.S` saving both and `fiber_init_stack` writing the declared values into a fresh 72-byte frame; [ADR-0033](decisions/0033-jobs-implementation-architecture.md) is amended. Four `[diag10c]` cases in crd-core-tests check the thread-start mode, the scoped round trip and the field-by-field comparison, and show that each compared MXCSR field changes a float result. **Value-domain probes and the generation-attributed result oracle landed locally** (2026-10-11, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-11-diag-10c-value-domains-and-result-oracle.md)): `crd/core/value_domain.hpp` declares a domain class by class (NaN, +Inf, -Inf, subnormals, -0) plus a closed numeric range (`any`, `finite` by default, `distance` admitting +Inf, `unit-interval`; an i64 `IntDomain`), and probes values from their bit patterns only, so a domain that allows a special value never reports it and no verdict depends on the caller's FTZ/DAZ/rounding (binary32 classified from its own bits and widened exactly). `crd/ceir/cook/result_oracle.hpp` judges a successful CEIR run's results against an independent reference or an integer invariant (CountMismatch, OutOfDomain, DiffersFromReference) and `ReloadSet::locate_result` attributes the first wrong result to the generation the handle names (current, retiring or gone) and the op that defined it in that generation's file; the correct generation is never blamed. Six `[diag10c]` cases in crd-core-tests and four in crd-ceir-cook-tests (a hot-swapped generation's wrong constant, a retiring plan's wrong op after the fix and after a drain, a wrapped square caught by an invariant on both executors, counts and invalid domains); twelve deliberate breaks each bit (eleven failed a case, one stopped on the debug build's bounds assertion). The CEIR executors are integer-only, so a CEIR plan run has no floating-point mode to probe. **Shape/stride, units/time-domain and float domains at the tensor and audio boundaries, and the mode probe at the audio callback and third-party calls, landed locally** (2026-10-11, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-11-diag-10c-tensor-and-audio-boundaries.md)): `crd/core/layout_probe.hpp` checks a strided view's claim (rank bound, element count and byte size in u64, first and last offsets in elements and bytes in i64 formed per dimension, named storage only when named, overlap only when proven and a violation only for a written view) and walks it against a `FloatDomain`, naming the first offender by coordinates and lane; `crd/hesap/tensor/probe.hpp` applies both to tensor views. DLPack import now refuses what the probe refuses; defects found and fixed there: a wrapping element count imported as an empty tensor, an offset past i64 imported, compact strides of an empty shape overflowed a signed product, a missing shape array was dereferenced and an address-space wrap imported; an expanded (stride-0) or empty capsule still imports. `crd/audio/audio_boundary.hpp`: a source binding declares its sample rate (0 = undeclared, unchecked, renders as before) and both renderers refuse a rate mismatch and a partial frame (defects: a ragged buffer's tail was dropped silently, a looped source of less than one frame divided by zero); `audio_sample_domain` names a non-finite sample on the bus; `render_audio_period` runs the device callback in the declared mode, keeps a mode it sets inside its period and reports both, and the WASAPI device counts divergent and non-finite periods (defect: a non-stereo endpoint got stereo written at its own channel stride; it now renders through a stereo scratch sized in `start()`). `call_keeping_fp_environment` reports and undoes a mode a foreign call leaves; a DLPack producer's deleter runs through it on every path. Sixteen deliberate breaks each failed a case (the partial-frame break was observed on two cases, one by the division-by-zero crash the fix prevents, and the missing-shape break by the access violation it prevents); the live device soak on this host ran 10 s at 48 kHz with zero divergent and zero non-finite periods. **Lifetime accounting beyond heap bytes landed locally** (2026-10-11, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-11-diag-10c-lifetime-accounting.md)): `crd/core/lifetime_ledger.hpp` counts, per class (FileHandle, LibraryHandle, MappedRegion with its bytes, DeviceObject, CallbackRegistration), acquisitions, matched releases, live, high water and live bytes with relaxed atomics in a constant-initialized table (no lock, no allocation); a release it cannot match changes nothing and is counted, so a window between two snapshots is Underflowed rather than wrapped, else Outstanding, Drained or Balanced, with per-class deltas and a one-line rendering. Wired: `vm::reserve`/`release` and the crd-jobs fiber stacks (MappedRegion), `DynamicLibrary` (LibraryHandle), `log::FileSink` open/close/rotation (FileHandle), the process-wide identity registry's Resource and Program identities (DeviceObject; Pass identities and a registry of one's own are not counted), and `EventBus` subscriptions (the bus is now move-only), `FileWatcher` entries, `ResourceManager` reload subscriptions, installed log sinks and the jobs observer (CallbackRegistration); handles opened and closed inside one call are scoped by rule and `crash.cpp` is not wired, both named in the design doc. `crd/core/os_resource_probe.hpp` is the independent oracle: whether this process holds a file (Windows: the process's own handle table, File-type disk handles by normalized final path; Linux: `/proc/self/fd` by device and inode) and how much of a range is reserved or mapped (VirtualQuery; `/proc/self/maps`), Unavailable with a reason where the OS cannot be asked. `[diag10c]` cases in crd-core-tests (five), crd-vm-tests (two), crd-jobs-tests (three: init/shutdown holds and returns exactly seven stacks, the observer, 32 jobs recording concurrently), crd-platform-tests (three), crd-log-tests (three, the file held and released as the OS sees it, also across a rotation), crd-app-tests (one), crd-resources-tests (one) and crd-gpu-context-tests (two, the ledger agreeing with the registry's `live_count`). **Queue pressure and exhausted budgets at the jobs and resource boundaries landed locally** (2026-10-11, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-11-diag-10c-queue-pressure.md)): `crd/core/budget_pressure.hpp` judges a bounded resource's `BudgetReading` (its bound or none, held now, the high water where the owner keeps it, refusals, soft-bound overruns) with integer arithmetic only: a level (Unread, Unbounded, Within, Near at 900 permille computed without an overflowing product, Full, Over) and a window verdict, worst first (Exhausted, Overrun, Saturated, Near, Relaxed only when a kept high water proves the peak below Near, else Undetermined; Unjudged when two readings cannot be compared). `crd::jobs::pressure_snapshot()` reports the counters, each fiber tier, each injection queue (no high water kept, so never Relaxed) and the pinned lanes, and `ResourceManager::memory_pressure()` the soft memory budget with its settled high water and overruns (all blocks pinned or held left it over the budget without a trace). Defects found and fixed: a full injection queue or local deque dropped the job where asserts are off, so its waiter hung; and each thread's pinned work was a single slot, so a second job pinned to a thread before it drained the first asserted or was overwritten and lost, reachable from authored CEIR with two `task.main_thread` tasks in flight (the new crd-ceir-host-tests case and a crd-jobs-tests case stopped on the assert on win-debug, and the jobs case hung on win-shipping until killed); the pinned lane is now a bounded MPMC queue (`Config::pinned_queue_capacity`) and every full queue or lane is a counted, always-on fatal ([ADR-0033](decisions/0033-jobs-implementation-architecture.md) amended). The queue-full specimen shows both refusals as Exhausted readings from inside the fatal, and the counter and fiber exhaustion specimens now also require theirs; eleven deliberate breaks each failed a case. (2026-10-11: the Visual Studio dialog that blocked reconfiguring the previous batch is gone; win-debug reconfigured normally.) **Warm/cold, soak, repeated-reload and shutdown workloads with one stressor at a time and seeded failure injection, measured slowdowns, and threads in the lifetime ledger landed locally** (2026-10-11, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-11-diag-10c-workloads.md)): `crd/core/workload_probe.hpp` runs cycles of setup, iterations and teardown (iteration 0 cold, the rest warm) and judges every iteration's result against what it should be (or cycle 0's cold reference), every seeded injected iteration (a pure function of seed, cycle and iteration; never the cold or the last one; always followed by a clean one) as detected, missed or never fired and the next as recovered or not, every cycle's lifetime-ledger window and progress against a bound; the verdict is the worst finding, located (SetupFailed, Diverged, FaultMissed, NotRecovered, IterationFailed, Leaked, Stalled, FaultNotFired, else Clean). Stressors are enumerated, and `attribute_finding` blames a variant's finding on a stressor only against a clean baseline that differs in exactly that one. `slowdown_report` classifies only from measurements (at least 8 samples a window, a baseline median of at least 1000 ns and an interquartile range within it; Slower or Faster only when the median moved past 250 permille AND the quartiles separate, else Inconclusive or Steady); hosted lanes judge results, lifetimes and progress, never speed, and the workloads print their timing verdict as evidence. Threads are the ledger's sixth class (the crd-jobs workers and hang watchdog, the asynchronous logger's worker, an inspect host's run, the diagnostic panel's request worker and the WASAPI render thread), judged against the OS by identity (thread id and start time; ended once it has exited, even unjoined). Workloads: crd-jobs-tests soaks three init/shutdown cycles of 64 parallel sums with a closed-form answer (every sum right, every window balanced, every worker the OS saw gone after its cycle; a 4-thread variant is clean, a variant with one 7 s delay is Stalled and attributed to Delay against a 5 s progress bound, the one wall-clock judgment the hosted lanes make); crd-resources-tests runs three fresh ResourceManagers through a cold load and 23 reloads each, with a memory-budget variant (clean, overruns counted) and failed-read and short-read fault-plan variants on the real I/O seam (every injected reload detected, last good mesh kept, recovered). Defect found and fixed by the jobs soak: on the default wake path a job pinned to a worker woke one arbitrary sleeper, so the target could sleep on with the job in its lane and its waiter hung (the 4-thread variant hung on win-debug; on the old scheduler a dedicated case lost the first job pinned to an idle worker); a pinned push now wakes every sleeper behind a fence, and a worker about to sleep wakes every sleeper when an announced sleeper holds pinned work ([ADR-0033](decisions/0033-jobs-implementation-architecture.md) amended). A second defect found by the new logger-thread case under linux-clang-tsan: `log::flush()` waited only for an empty queue, but the worker pops a record before it takes the sink lock, so flush could return before the last record was written; it now also waits for the record being delivered (a swept-race case: 4000 rounds of log then flush). Eighteen of twenty deliberate breaks failed a case; removing either half of the pinned-wake fix alone does not (each half closes the common case; together they close the window the other leaves). **Driver/device-reset and host-pressure evidence, the GPU side of pressure and the mode witness around driver calls landed locally** (2026-10-12, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-12-diag-10c-device-and-host-pressure.md)): `crd/core/host_pressure.hpp` reads the host's physical memory, commit charge (bounded only where the OS enforces it: Windows always, Linux in strict overcommit) and this process's resident set with its peak as `BudgetReading`s, unread with a reason where the OS cannot answer; the usable RAM agrees with a second OS interface. `IGpuContext::device_memory()` reads the OS's per-process budget and usage of the device's adapter (DX12: DXGI `QueryVideoMemoryInfo`, local and non-local; Vulkan: `VK_EXT_memory_budget`, now enabled whenever advertised), and an absent segment (WARP's non-local 0/0) stays unread, never Full; usage follows a committed 256 MiB buffer and back on the RTX 4070 Ti SUPER and on WARP through DXGI and on the RTX driver through the Vulkan budget, while llvmpipe advertises the extension but reports a usage that does not follow allocations (its test says so instead of calling it tracked). `IFrameGraph::transient_pressure()` reports the transient budget (bound, footprint, high water, one refusal per refused build) and `gpu.resources` now reports each context's device memory and each frame graph's transient budget instead of `heap_usage: "unavailable"`. `crd/gpu/driver_witness.hpp` runs instance and device creation, dxc and shaderc, `ExecuteCommandLists`/`vkQueueSubmit` and both presents under the numerical-mode witness (a mode a call leaves is put back and counted per kind with the first offender; none seen on the RTX, WARP or llvmpipe). Each backend takes the host and device pressure with the loss's sequence when it records a device lost, and `attribute_device_fault` calls a failure an EngineDefect only when the same inputs fail on another configuration (Injected for a simulated one; else PressureCoincident at a Full or Over reading, NotReproduced, or Undiscriminated). Defect found and fixed by the transient-budget cases: a second `build()` of one recording placed the transients over the first build's, leaking them on DX12 with their heaps and the device (DXGI usage stayed 32 MiB up after the graph died, and the next test's validation-enabled device creation failed) and binding memory to already-bound images on Vulkan (a 16 MiB leak on the RTX budget); a frame graph now builds once per recording on both backends and a second build without `reset()` is refused (not a budget refusal). Fourteen deliberate breaks each failed a case. **GPU queue depth, the native owners in the lifetime ledger and their shutdown landed locally** (2026-10-12, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-12-diag-10c-queue-depth-and-native-owners.md)): `crd/gpu/queue_pressure.hpp` (crd-gpu-context, device-free) counts a step in flight from the completion seam that queued it until a seam observed it; a timeline observed through a value retires its step and every earlier step on its queue (fence-less ones included), and a loss, a forgotten queue or device, or a timeline that starts again abandons, counted; a completion with nothing pending is unmatched, and a step the fixed table cannot hold leaves the reading unread. The DX12 seams (`dx12_submit`, `dx12_signal`, `dx12_wait`, every removal) and the Vulkan seam (`vk_submit`, both fence waits, both idle waits, the first loss, `vk_forget_device`) feed it; each DX12 context forgets its queue, and a private-data interface on each DX12 device ends its counts when D3D12 destroys it. `IGpuContext::queue_pressure()` (appended, default unread) reads it as an unbounded `BudgetReading`, and `gpu.resources` reports each context's `queue_*` fields and `queue_depth_read`. A synchronous context never leaves a step in flight, the DX12 deferred frame graph leaves one frame and the Vulkan graph's two-slot ring at most two. Two more ledger classes (eight, filling the u8 masks): NativeGpuObject (the DX12 device reference per device scope, created queues, fences and the swapchain; the crd-kir-dx12 backend's device, queue and fence; the Vulkan instance, device, every fence and swapchain) and OsObject (the GLFW window, every fence event, the WASAPI enumerator, endpoint, audio client, render client and period event); `LifetimeHold` records a release that is implicit. Shutdown workloads (3 DX12 and 3 Vulkan cycles of create, four round trips and destroy; window cycles; audio stop and three restarts) leave every cycle Balanced; the OS judges the window (FindWindow, the USER-object count). Defects found and fixed: a WASAPI start after stop opened a second session over the stopped one and leaked it (ten OS objects instead of five); and a DX12 device's queue counts outlived it, so a later device at the same address inherited a lost reading (three new cases failed in the whole DX12 program until the device-end watch); and a simulated Vulkan loss let the teardown that followed destroy objects in-flight work still used (lavapipe leaked a worker allocation under LeakSanitizer) until the seam drained the real device after recording a simulated loss. Twenty-two deliberate breaks each failed a case (twenty-one on win-debug, one on linux-gcc-asan). **Remaining:** only the hosted run, which must show crd-core-tests (forty `[diag10c]` cases, including the two host-pressure cases and the native-class and `LifetimeHold` case), crd-jobs-tests (eighteen, including the queue-full specimen in both modes, the concurrent pinned pushes and the workload soak under linux-clang-tsan, and the pinned idle-worker case), crd-ceir-host-tests (one), crd-ceir-cook-tests (five), crd-hesap-tensor-io-tests (five), crd-audio-tests (eight: the seven plus the device-lifetime case, whose refused start must balance on every hosted lane; | 094 | <a id="slice-simd-dispatch"></a>**SIMD-DISPATCH** | Partial | x64 SSE2 (the x86-64 baseline) stays a supported CPU floor through runtime dispatch (user decision 2026-10-26; it replaces DIAG.11b follow-up (r)'s one-AVX2-level plan). All general engine code builds at the baseline ISA. Hot kernels build once per level (SSE2, SSE4.2, AVX2/FMA, AVX-512/AVX10 on x64; NEON and SVE/SVE2 on ARM64 under their own release rows) in isolated kernel units, and one startup selection reads CPUID plus OS-enabled state (XSAVE/XCR0, hybrid cores) with a forced-level override for tests. A guard proves no shared inline body or COMDAT reaches a baseline library from a higher-ISA unit on MSVC, clang-cl, GCC and Clang (the 2026-10-26 LTCG inlining defect). ADR-0063 determinism: declared bit-exact kernels agree across every level, the rest stay within declared tolerances against oracles. One binary runs every level as a forced-level CI arm; AVX-512 kernels are proven under Intel SDE until hardware exists (SDE 10.13.1 approved by the user and installed on this host 2026-10-27, no longer waiting on the user). Every affected board (diag-overhead, hesap, geometry, jobs) is re-measured at each level against its peers. **Contract, detection and selection landed** (2026-10-26, [session](sessions/2026-10-26-simd-dispatch-cpu-detection.md)): [ADR-0134](decisions/0134-runtime-cpu-dispatch.md) decides every clause's mechanism; `crd/core/cpu_features.hpp` is the only CPUID/XGETBV site (TickClock reads it), decodes 45 features with their XCR0 state, AVX10 version and width, APX and hybrid core types, intersects every CPU the process may run on and applies `CRD_CPU_LEVEL` (refused above the hardware), judged against the OS view on Windows and Linux with six teeth. **Kernel units landed** (2026-10-26, [session](sessions/2026-10-26-simd-dispatch-kernel-units.md)): `crd_add_cpu_kernels` builds a family once per level in its own object library with that level's flags, `CRD_MATH_LEVEL_NS` keeps every shared inline function per level, `crd/math/kernel_dispatch.hpp` resolves one table from the selection and the build's cap, and the batch small-float conversions are the first family (portable and AVX2 bodies, bit-identical to the scalar converts on every level the host runs, forced-level `crd-math-kernels-at-<level>` CTests, six teeth, board at parity with HEAD). **Level-aware types landed** (2026-10-27, [session](sessions/2026-10-27-simd-dispatch-level-aware-types.md)): `backend.hpp` keys the backend on the unit's level (an SSE4.2 backend; `CRD_SIMD_HAS_*` rungs replace `CRD_SIMD_BACKEND`), every SIMD type, the f64 exp/log cores and their AVX2 twins live in `CRD_MATH_LEVEL_NS` and call no standard-library inline function (`crd/math/libm.hpp`), `kNativeLaneWidth` is 8 on every level, and a 94-operation probe compiled per level proves every level the host runs gives the portable bits (six cross-level defects fixed, eight teeth, linux-gcc-debug too). **Stats kernels landed** (2026-10-27, [session](sessions/2026-10-27-simd-dispatch-hesap-stats-kernels.md)): the Philox and Threefry fills and the Student-t score reduction are the second family, bit-exact on every level (eleven teeth, linux-gcc-debug too), the AVX2 fills 1.76x and 1.85x HEAD (Philox 2.1x NumPy), Student-t at HEAD parity and 2.5x JAX; a dense case holds dot and gemv rows of only -0 products to +0 on every level. **512-bit types landed** (2026-10-28, [session](sessions/2026-10-28-simd-dispatch-avx512-types.md)): `Vec16f`, `Vec8d` and `Vec16i` are one zmm register at avx512 and two 256-bit halves below it (outside the `simd.hpp` umbrella), with all-ones lane masks, the halves' pairwise horizontal sum and masked partial loads and stores; `backend_name()` is "AVX-512" there; the level probe holds them to the portable bits on every level, avx512 under SDE skx; `crd_log8`/`crd_exp8` are the eight-lane twins of the scalar cores, bit-identical with them. **Dense and direct zmm bodies landed** (2026-10-28, [session](sessions/2026-10-28-simd-dispatch-avx512-dense-direct.md)): at avx512 the dense and direct vector steps run on `Vec8d` and `Vec16f` (one ZMM) and the GEMM on a 14-row tile of 28 ZMM accumulators (f64 14 by 16, f32 14 by 32, prefetching two lines a step), with avx2's bits (one fused step per element); the dot-shaped reductions take a third declared shape (w = 8 and 16, the halves' pairwise lane sum), within the inner-product bound of avx2; the Mc and Nc blocks round down to whole tiles of the level's shape; direct sums 16 panel columns a group with unchanged bits; both families pass under SDE skx; tests on hosted CI, boards in the row-close pass; a hosted AVX-512 runner took the CG moat to the rounding floor of f, where the Wolfe search failed, and the search now tests Armijo as a difference and judges trials f cannot rank by φ' (Hager-Zhang approximate Wolfe, [finding](sessions/2026-10-28-simd-dispatch-avx512-dense-direct.md#a-hosted-avx-512-runner-the-wolfe-search-at-the-rounding-floor-of-f)). **Sparse zmm bodies landed** (2026-10-28, [session](sessions/2026-10-28-simd-dispatch-avx512-sparse.md)): at avx512 a slice pair runs the columns both slices store in one ZMM (f64 and f32 gathering both slices' x in one instruction, complex f32 both slices' values), then each slice finishes in the 256-bit body with opmask gathers; a complex f64 slice fills one ZMM; every level keeps the CSR bits; passes under SDE skx. **Stats zmm bodies landed** (2026-10-28, [session](sessions/2026-10-28-simd-dispatch-avx512-stats.md)): at avx512 Philox runs 48 blocks a step in three groups of sixteen (shared with hesap-tensor), Threefry 24 in three groups of eight with `vprolq`, Student-t eight terms a step added half by half to its four lanes; every level keeps the portable bits; passes under SDE skx. **Special zmm body landed** (2026-10-28, [session](sessions/2026-10-28-simd-dispatch-avx512-special.md)): the Lanczos bodies are written once over a register width; avx512 runs eight lanes with `crd_log8`/`crd_exp8`, then one four-lane register, then the scalar loop, with the scalar functions' bits; passes under SDE skx. **Tensor zmm bodies landed** (2026-10-28, [session](sessions/2026-10-28-simd-dispatch-avx512-tensor.md)): avx512 runs the permute squares on zmm (a streamed row off a line splits into two 32-byte stores), three binned streams of eight lanes, sixteen-lane quantizers, eight-lane softmax, the Q8_0 dots two blocks a zmm in the integer stage with each block's f32 combine in block order, and the int8 dots 64 values or 16 outputs a step; the avx512+avx512vnni variant runs them on `vpdpbusd`; `crd_add_kernel_level_tests` takes per-suite `SDE_CPUS`, and the tensor and tensor-nn suites add spr; every table keeps the portable bits under SDE skx and spr. **float_convert zmm body landed** (2026-10-28, [session](sessions/2026-10-28-simd-dispatch-avx512-float-convert.md)): the integer transcription runs on a lane-mask type (opmasks at avx512, unchanged instructions below), sixteen lanes with a masked last step instead of a scalar tail; | 100 | <a id="slice-hw-resilience.1"></a>**HW-RESILIENCE.1** | Open | Data integrity on faulty hardware (user decision 2026-10-26: even faulty hardware must work gracefully). Every cooked asset, compressed block, network packet and saved document carries a checksum verified after read and after decompression; a mismatch retries once from the source, then fails with a typed error and a clear message, never a crash or silent bad data. Saves are atomic with checksums and keep previous generations, with autosave and journaling so a crash costs seconds of work. Adversarial tests flip bits in each path and prove detection, retry and recovery. **Research amendment** (2026-10-27, [proposal](research/2026-10-27-networking-and-crash-pipeline-2026-comparison.md#p-15)): The network checksum under encryption: the AEAD tag already detects corruption in flight, so the added check is a plaintext integrity hash computed at serialisation and verified after decryption (it catches a sender's own memory or pipeline fault that AEAD would seal as valid), plus state hashes for lockstep and rollback. One foundation-owned, dispatched checksum family replaces the three CRC-32 copies in `perf`, `resources` and `hesap-tensor` under [OWN.1](#slice-own.1): CRC-32/IEEE (the PNG, ZIP and gzip polynomial) with carry-less multiply and portable paths, CRC32C with SSE4.2, carry-less multiply and portable paths, and a 64-bit fast hash, each built per SIMD-DISPATCH level with byte-identical results. **Research amendment** (2026-10-27, [proposal](research/2026-10-27-publishing-packaging-and-app-management-2026-comparison.md#p-41)): The same checksum family covers installers, patches and update payloads; repair re-fetches only bad chunks. | [SIMD-DISPATCH](#slice-simd-dispatch) | [Detail](design/runtime-diagnostics.md); [ADR-0133](decisions/0133-runtime-diagnostics-and-instrumentation.md); [Decisions](sessions/2026-10-26-user-decisions-platform-floors-and-research.md); [Evidence](sessions/2026-10-26-catch2-fault-address.md); [Adoption](sessions/2026-10-27-research-adopt-part-4.md); [Adoption](sessions/2026-10-27-research-adopt-part-5.md) |

| 105 | <a id="slice-diag.11b"></a>**DIAG.11b** | Partial | Measured disabled/basic/full overhead, focused local routes, tiered sanitizer/race/fuzz CI and investigation runbooks; DG18. **Overhead harness, event-site form and first boards landed locally** (2026-10-16, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-16-diag-11b-overhead-harness.md), [board](bench/2026-10-16-diag-11b-overhead.md)): `CRD_FLIGHT_RECORD` evaluates a site's payload only when a recorder runs and its detail keeps the event (`FlightRecorder::admit`), and `record()` drops a left-out event before the clock or the ring mutex; side-effect and no-wait cases (`[diag11b]`) with teeth. `crd-diag-overhead` (`tests/support/diag-overhead`) measures the workloads alloc, jobs, offline and events in the modes off, basic and full, one process each, with the authored `overhead_basic`/`overhead_full` flight policies and `overhead_offline.ceir`; its 12 `crd-diag-overhead-*` CTests hold the structural half on every lane (off evaluates no payload and starts no diagnostic thread, basic filters every event, full records every one, every capture delivered, the lifetime ledger balanced). `scripts/diag-overhead.py` interleaves processes and judges ADR-0133 ID-5 (within, over, or unresolved as a loss; `test-diag-overhead.py` covers it; ID-5 amended with the workload deviations). Boards on win-shipping-profile against win-shipping, linux-gcc-shipping and linux-gcc-relwithdebinfo: storage within everywhere. **The installed application's sites** (2026-10-16, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-16-diag-11b-installed-sites.md)): `diag-consumer` writes every event site with `CRD_FLIGHT_RECORD` and formats a message only inside it (`site_text`, counted); `crd-package-consumer` runs the failure at the full and the basic detail and holds `CONSUMER_SITES` and the bundle to the kept events (40 of 40 formatted and recorded at full; 5 of 40 at basic, the 35 informational orders left out unformatted, the bundle holding the five refunds); an eager site fails the basic arm (formatted 40, expected 5). **The shipping lane's link-time warnings** (2026-10-17, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-17-diag-11b-link-time-warnings.md)): the hosted linux-gcc-shipping lane's 44 GCC LTO diagnostics (13 sites) and 35 `lto-wrapper` lines are repaired with nothing suppressed: `swap_last2` bounded by `kMaxRank`, `pop_back` trims in the ceridc diag tests, a non-negative node count in `eval_cpu`, closed-form ends of `pack_b`'s interleave and `convert_f32_to_f16`'s vector part, the heterogeneous `CommandRegistry::find`, and for the two DIAG false positives a clear-then-copy `set_path` and `String::append`'s heap contract after `reserve`; the zstd IPO guard names the real `libzstd_static` (it never applied) and zstd's unused legacy decoders are off. A WSL relink of all 189 executables of the configuration prints no warning (before: all 44 reproduced). **Warnings held at zero** (2026-10-17, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-17-diag-11b-warning-gates.md)): GCC and Clang link lines carry `-Werror` under the same switch as the compile lines (`crd-warnings`' link options; probes showed GCC judges link-time optimization's diagnostics by the link line alone and `lto-wrapper`'s notices ignore it), and full builds of linux-gcc-release, linux-gcc-relwithdebinfo and linux-gcc-shipping link every executable under it with no warning (a restored `set_path` false positive fails the link); crd-jobs' MSVC `/Od` pin compiles in `engine/foundation/jobs/unoptimized/` without the configuration's `/O2`, so win-shipping, win-shipping-profile and win-release no longer print D9025, with the pinned code unchanged (disassembly and symbols of all 14 pinned objects on four lanes), and `crd-check-compile-commands` fails any cl.exe/clang-cl command carrying two optimization levels on every Windows Ninja lane (teeth: the strip turned off fails it). win-clang-cl-shipping's two zstd `-Wunused-function` were left for their own batch (below). **The warning set at the link** (2026-10-17, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-17-diag-11b-link-time-warning-set.md)): probes showed GCC's link-time compiler takes no warning option from the objects and `lto-wrapper` forwards no C-family option, `-Wall` included, so a `-Wall`-class defect exposed only by cross-file inlining linked green; the GCC link line now names the compile set's options lto1 reads (`-Wextra -Wpedantic -Wshadow` and `-Wall`'s members, `-Warray-bounds=1` and `-Wmaybe-uninitialized` among them; `-Wrestrict`, `-Wdangling-pointer`, `-Wmismatched-new-delete` and the format-overflow class cannot reach it on GCC 13.3), and GLFW builds without IPO on GCC so its code never meets them. The 14 sites the set found on the three IPO trees are repaired, none suppressed: real ones in the CKIR scan builders (a per-thread chunk outside 1..64 read an unset register or wrote past it, now refused), einsum's plan (no step count after saturated greedy sweeps), `HashMap::operator[]` (an unset index on a corrupt table, now fatal) and a test artifact's unset member; the rest restated so the bounds are visible. A cross-file out-of-bounds read links green under the old line and fails the link under the set (teeth). `-Wnull-dereference` reached lto1 too and was left for its own batch. **Link-time null dereferences** (2026-10-17, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-17-diag-11b-link-time-null-dereference.md)): the GCC link line now carries `-Wnull-dereference`, and its 80 link-time locations (six collection rounds on linux-gcc-shipping, the stubborn links relinked with `-flto-partition=one` to list every site) and the 42 more linux-gcc-relwithdebinfo shows with asserts compiled in (an ignorable assert keeps the null arm) are repaired, none suppressed. Lookups an invariant makes certain, which followed a null after an assert that compiles out, gained invariant accessors fatal in every build with no added compare on the hot path (`ComponentRegistry::require_info`, `ArchetypeGraph::require`, `HashMap::at`, `toml::node::child_at`, `func::func_body`; probe disassembly: the same 11 branches in each scene accessor). Allocation refusals are the named out-of-memory fatal through `construct.hpp`'s new `*_or_fatal` helpers: the CEIR context's IR arena, and the containers, which adopted a null buffer (a refused `Array` growth was relocated into null and kept its capacity; `String`, `HashMap`, `RingBuffer`, `SpscQueue`, `AtomicArray`, `ConcurrentQueue` likewise), and `allocate_array` refuses a byte size above `PTRDIFF_MAX` (the release tree's one new link-time warning, a memset bound GCC derived from the checked size in `dlasd1`, which now makes dlasd1.f's argument checks). Real defects: `TransformPropagation` dereferenced a `ChildOf` child without a `Transform` and never recomputed a dirty leaf under a dirty organisation node; the transform writers wrote through null on a dead entity or a missing `Transform`; `Commands::add_component` of an unregistered type read a null `ComponentInfo`; the renderer read a resource handle's payload twice; `TlsfAllocator`'s borrowing constructor wrote its sentinels through a null buffer; the authored rewrite driver's build action followed a missing definer; `smoke_mesh`'s checks could never fail a release run; test oracles dereferenced nullable lookups. A null lineage map handed to `expand_ml_ops`' driver made IPA-CP specialise `HashMap::rehash` for a null `this` (the link's IPA-CP dump names the call); the driver takes a recorder callable. The crash specimens' deliberate null writes go through a volatile pointer (GCC had rewritten them into its own trap). Tests with teeth: three `[organisation]` transform cases; contract-fatal CTests in child processes (`crd_diag_fatal_tests`: `crd-containers-fatal-*` 9, `crd-scene-fatal-*` 6, `crd-ceir-fatal-*` 5, `crd-toml-fatal-*` 1, and five alloc-fatal specimen modes for the helpers and the borrowed buffer), each failing or crashing with its check removed; reverting one repair fails the shipping link under the new line and links green under the old. **zstd's clang-cl and configure warnings; where a pause lands** (2026-10-17, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-17-diag-11b-zstd-configure-and-pause-landing.md)): a sweep of every hosted job log of run 38640651640 found, besides the warnings repaired above, zstd 1.5.5's configure deprecation on all 21 build jobs, CMP0194 on the 10 MSVC jobs, two unused `_NOTE_*` preset variables and win-clang-cl-shipping's two zstd `-Wunused-function`; all reproduced locally from fresh configures. No zstd release (v1.5.7, dev) changes the `__GNUC__` gate on `MEM_STATIC`'s unused attribute, so two registered patches on build-owned copies (`cmake/patches/zstd-*-unused.cmake`, swapped into `libzstd_static`'s sources) give the two assert-only helpers the attribute under clang-cl only; the objects are the upstream objects (identical code on win-clang-cl-shipping, win-shipping-profile and linux-gcc-shipping; with asserts only the asserts' line numbers move). `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM` 3.10 ends the deprecation on CMake 4 (zstd sets `cmake_policy(VERSION 3.13.0)` itself), CMP0194 is answered `OLD` for zstd's directory under both its names (CMake 4.1 to 4.3 read the default as `CMP194`, probed), and the preset notes became `description`s; the three fresh configures and every lane's zstd build then print nothing. The DIAG.8b pause case's oracle expected `NotYetComputed` for whatever op a pause held, but a request lands at the next safe point before any instr in any frame, and `core.for` defines no result (`NoSuchValue`), where a slow TSan thread had landed: the case asserts the landing rule, and a new case pins landings on `core.for`, the loop body and the callee through the session's observer (teeth: the old oracle, an executor that skips resultless instrs, a `read_value` that counts the held instr as run; 100 TSan repeats clean). The edit exposed one link-time `-Wnull-dereference` in `test_hello.cpp` (an unchecked `func_body_block`), repaired with `func::func_body`. **Allocation refusals in the scene and the resource manager** (2026-10-17, committed, not pushed; [session](sessions/2026-10-17-diag-11b-unchecked-allocations.md)): follow-up (h) and the same shape swept through the scene, resources and memory modules. The four test sites that test the lookup and the seven engine sites that branch on it keep it. `crd-ceir-invariants` gains I7: every `func_body_block` call in engine, tests, tools, runtime and sandbox tests its result against nullptr on its line or through its variable within six lines (teeth: an assigned, a returned and a chained unchecked lookup and a removed `REQUIRE` each fail both scripts, under gawk, mawk and PowerShell 5.1). A machine-readable register beside the module registry lists every protocol, extension and algorithm Cerid implements or plans (RFC or draft and its revision, IANA codepoints, owning module, implementation state, interop evidence, deprecation date) and a watch list (multipath QUIC, reliable reset, address discovery, ACK frequency, receive timestamps, QUIC-LB, WebTransport, connect-udp-listen, MoQ transport, RTP over QUIC, qlog, Opus DRED, MTC, NIST IR 8547). Crypto agility by registry: algorithms are identified, never hard-coded; hybrids are the default; the accepted set is a signed policy generation swapped live, with dated migration windows, an offline grace period and a remote, signed disable for a broken algorithm (RFC 7696 is the checklist); crypto, congestion-control, NAT-traversal, codec, fleet and matchmaking providers sit behind owned interfaces, and swapping one never changes the wire format. Long-lived artefacts (replays, crash packs, qlog and pcapng captures, world journals) carry schema versions with N-1 readers (OPS.2 owns the N-1 bundle reader). A CTest fails when a pinned draft has expired or a pinned RFC is obsoleted in the committed register snapshot. A scheduled re-research (a light scan after each IETF meeting, a full run once a year or when a pinned item changes status) proposes amendments for the user and never edits rows itself; snapshot updates that need a download are listed for the user's approval first. NET.5 and every later networked row cite the register entries they implement. Keep handshakes within QUIC's amplification limit with certificate compression (RFC 8879), address-validation tokens and resumption, measured in round trips, and raw public keys or pinned Cerid credentials for game and session servers. Support ECH (RFC 9849) on public endpoints. Bind the Tamarin/ProVerif model to the code by generating the handshake state machine from one description or checking it by state learning against the model. Choose verified primitives (HACL*, libcrux, AWS-LC's mlkem-native) behind the provider interface, never written in-house. Hardware-backed keys (TPM 2.0, Secure Enclave, Android Keystore, YubiKey-class keys) with software fallback; rotation and revocation rehearsed in NET-SIM. RFC 9850 key logging and all NET-DEBUG capture keys are compiled out of shipping builds and refused at runtime when built in, enforced by a CI guard that mirrors [SCRIPT.4](#slice-script.4)'s allowlists. Cryptography export control is [COMPLY.1](#slice-comply.1)'s.
