| 233 | <a id="slice-jobs-hard.3"></a>**JOBS-HARD.3** | Open | Full task/allocator/CEIR consumer board: actual pool utilization, oversubscription, single-worker progress and cross-platform soak. Reuse DIAG mechanisms; qualify broader/new product consumers and targets here. Also owned (2026-10-25, [DIAG.11b](#slice-diag.11b) clause (8)): the fiber pool's shared free list contended. In the overhead harness's tiny-job workload (2048 jobs a frame, eight threads on 16 logical processors) `FiberPool::acquire` held 53% of the off arm's sampled CPU, 37% on the instruction after the Treiber head's `lock cmpxchg` ([board](bench/2026-10-25-diag-11b-external-sampling.md)). **Fixed the same day** (1a12466c, e0de26cc, cdcc3e79; [session](sessions/2026-10-25-jobs-fiber-pool-contention.md), [bench](bench/2026-10-25-jobs-fiber-pool-contention.md), [ADR-0033](decisions/0033-jobs-implementation-architecture.md) decisions 8 and 9): a thread keeps its completed job's fiber, still acquired, for its next new job of the same tier, and returns it before a resume, before a job of another tier, just before it blocks waiting for work, when it leaves its loop, when the main thread's `wait()` or pump returns and at shutdown, so the pool's readings stay exact and the sizing bound (parked fibers plus threads) is unchanged; an idle-fiber cache was rejected because its high water cannot be exact without a global update per acquire. `jobs::run` of a span now wakes once per batch with at most one token per thread: the token and wake per job had left up to 2048 tokens a frame for idle workers to spin through and cost a futex syscall per job, which made linux-gcc-shipping's off 25% slower once the pool no longer paced the consumers. The free list is reached about once per thread per frame (203, 207 and 50 to 124 acquisitions for 409,600 jobs at four, eight and sixteen threads). Against the build before: win-shipping-profile off -39.9% frame and -42.4% CPU at four threads on 5555, -50.2% / -67.0% at eight and -88.6% / -86.2% at sixteen; linux-gcc-shipping's profiling twin -46.1% / -57.1%, -46.8% / -68.6% and -98.0% / -87.6%; basic and full alike; cachegrind -13.0% instructions a frame at one thread and -56% at four; off over compiled-out +0.00% in instructions. Correct on win-debug, win-asan, linux-gcc-debug, linux-gcc-asan and linux-clang-tsan, repeated and under a pinned busy-loop neighbour, with new cases and teeth (`test_fiber_keep.cpp`, `test_batch_wake.cpp`). Outside readers no longer race a restart (0e1433ef): every snapshot pins the pool, `shutdown()` closes it and waits for pinned readers before freeing anything, a closed pool reads as one before `init()`, and `test_diag_snapshot_restart.cpp` crashed four of four runs on win-asan and on win-debug with the old guard. The streaming case's remaining linux-clang-tsan fault is this host's: values no store wrote (a `{pid, uid}` word, instruction bytes, a null `unique_ptr::get()` of a held array), no signal before it, and a Cerid-free control of the same shape faults too, also with no fiber at all (300 interleaved rounds: the case 41, the fiber control 30, the plain control 24; the plain control unsanitized 0 of 250 beside 5 of 250 under TSan); hosted linux-clang-tsan passed the case. `host-check.yml` gained two dispatch-only TSan legs (`scripts/tsan-host-check.py`, 150 pinned rounds each of the case and the control's three arms) that settle it on hosted machines. **Fewer processors than threads** (2026-10-26, [session](sessions/2026-10-26-jobs-fiber-keep-oversubscription.md)): complete run 40274818980 failed the short-frames case on the hosted 4-vCPU Windows runner (17,524 acquisitions for 25,600 jobs, 0.68 a job; the 140,192 in the check is that times 8). The hook fired only before real sleeps; a pusher slower than the workers made them sleep between nearly every two jobs. A worker that keeps a fiber now spins for a token (128 turns of pauses and a yield, a read of the count, the protocol unchanged) before it gives the fiber back: 50 to 67 acquisitions at one to eight processors on win-debug, 53 to 179 at two to eight on linux-gcc-debug and 567 to 831 at one (bound 3,200; teeth 8 of 8 on both); a new case pins the pool to one and two processors itself. win-shipping-profile jobs board neutral at four and eight threads, -12.8% frame and +17.6% CPU at four threads on two processors; the case is 1.6x slower on linux-gcc-debug at one processor (recorded trade). Left here: the dispatched host check, and the scheduler's single shared injection queue under one producer, which this did not measure beyond the jobs workload. | [JOBS-HARD.2](#slice-jobs-hard.2) | [Detail](research/2026-09-12-cerid-whole-system-review.md#finding-g03); [ADR-0130](decisions/0130-system-qualification-and-agent-driven-products.md); [G03](research/2026-09-12-cerid-whole-system-review.md#finding-g03); [Diagnostic foundation](design/runtime-diagnostics.md#existing-programme-ownership-after-diag) |

The European Accessibility Act (Directive (EU) 2019/882, applied since 2025-06-28: e-commerce services such as storefronts and purchase flows, electronic communications with real-time text, e-books) with EN 301 549 and WCAG 2.2 AA; the ADA and Section 508 for engineering products sold to US public bodies; the CVAA (47 CFR Part 14) for communication functions; the UK Equality Act 2010. Turkish block: Law No. 5378 on Persons with Disabilities and its accessibility rules for information and communication services. Delivers: the conformance matrix (requirement, owning feature, automated and screen-reader test), accessibility statements per product, and the facts the store kit turns into accessibility labels; a CTest fails a surface that regresses a mapped requirement. Each instrument is read in its current consolidated text from its primary source (official journal or regulator) and dated in the [COMPLY.0](#slice-comply.0) register before this row closes; every obligation gets its owning row and a check that proves it; interpretation that needs counsel is a recorded counsel review item, never guessed. Rules are authored CHIR assets swapped live per jurisdiction as reviewed generations; COMPLY owns rules, checks and shared generators, and the governed rows consume them. Registrations, filings and accounts are user actions taken by the publisher (the user's Turkish company) after everything is implemented and qualified; they never block implementation. | [COMPLY.0](#slice-comply.0) | [Detail](research/2026-10-27-publishing-packaging-and-app-management-2026-comparison.md#area-7-compliance-legal); [ADR-0107](decisions/0107-ui-2d-architecture.md); [ADR-0130](decisions/0130-system-qualification-and-agent-driven-products.md); [Adoption](sessions/2026-10-27-research-adopt-comply-family.md) |

Pack contents are untrusted data under [AGENT.3](#slice-agent.3) (its hostile-input corpus covers prompt injection through crash logs, asset names and plugin metadata). The store is an OpenID Connect provider: Cerid-built products, [MCP-ADAPT](#slice-mcp-adapt)'s remote sign-in under [AGENT.3](#slice-agent.3)'s OAuth profile and the SHIP.9 hub sign in with one Cerid account. Family accounts: parental control of account settings, spending limits and approval of every paid transaction (the Law No. 5651 game-platform duties from 2026-11-01), play-time and rating limits, and family library sharing where the publisher's terms allow it, from [COMPLY.8](#slice-comply.8)'s kit; age signals and age assurance only where the register requires them, with the data minimised. KVKK: the notice (aydınlatma metni) and each explicit consent shown separately, commercial-message consent recorded through İYS (Law No. 6563), and self-service access, correction, export and deletion with the retention rules of [COMPLY.2](#slice-comply.2); the same under GDPR when the store enters the EU. Developer and seller accounts verify identity, company and tax records (trader traceability where the register requires it) and bind to [DATA-TRUST.2](#slice-data-trust.2)'s publisher identity. Account screens are accessible ([COMPLY.7](#slice-comply.7)) and localized, Turkish first ([I18N.1](#slice-i18n.1)). Peers: Steam and Epic accounts for sign-in time and takeover resistance; FIDO2 conformance tools are a download the user approves first. | 693 | <a id="slice-store.2"></a>**STORE.2** | Open | Catalogue, storefront and discovery. Product pages come from [SHIP.6](#slice-ship.6)'s authored, localized store-metadata asset (one asset feeds Steam, the other stores and the Cerid store): media, descriptions, system requirements checked against the visitor's machine (CPU level from [SIMD-DISPATCH](#slice-simd-dispatch), GPU tier from [GPU-TIER.0](#slice-gpu-tier.0)), languages and accessibility features ([A11Y-GAME](#slice-a11y-game)), the age rating (IARC and the regional boards now, the Turkish rating when ICTA publishes its scheme) and the data and AI disclosures COMPLY.8 generates. Prices show in Turkish lira, tax-inclusive, with the real-currency price beside any virtual currency. Search and filters, tags, curated lists, sales and event calendars, bundles, wishlists and gifts; recommendations need consent, explain themselves and offer an order without profiling (DSA recommender transparency once the store enters the EU), with no dark patterns. Reviews come only from verified owners, with review-bombing detection in `hesap-stats`, developer replies, and removal through [COMPLY.5](#slice-comply.5)'s notice-and-action contract with statements of reasons. The desktop storefront is a crd-ui surface of the store client ([STORE.4](#slice-store.4)); the web storefront is rendered by the store services, works without scripts, runs under a strict content security policy with no third-party scripts or trackers, and meets WCAG 2.2 AA and the EAA's e-commerce duties ([COMPLY.7](#slice-comply.7)); the WASM client joins in [STORE-WEB](#slice-store-web). Layouts are authored assets swapped live. Orders are the store's; money and entitlements stay [SHIP.7](#slice-ship.7)'s one owner, with no second payment path. Turkish payment service providers licensed under Law No. 6493 connect through SHIP.7's adapters, with 3-D Secure and hosted payment fields or redirects, so card data never reaches Cerid and the PCI DSS scope stays at the smallest self-assessment; refunds and chargebacks revoke entitlements through SHIP.7. Each sale issues an e-archive invoice (an e-invoice for registered business buyers) through an integrator authorised by the Revenue Administration (GİB), with KDV (20% today) computed from the register's rate entries; the digital service tax thresholds (Law No. 7194) and other countries' VAT regimes are register entries read when a country opens. Law No. 6502 and the Distance Contracts Regulation: the pre-contract information and the distance contract are shown before payment and delivered on a durable medium; the 14-day withdrawal right applies, and its waiver for instantly delivered digital content is offered only with the consent and disclosure the regulation requires; the store's own refund policy above it is an authored asset. Parental approval of paid transactions ([STORE.1](#slice-store.1)), odds disclosure and the per-jurisdiction rules on paid random items come from [COMPLY.8](#slice-comply.8). Gift cards and a store wallet exist only in a design the register's Law No. 6493 electronic-money entries allow (counsel review). Fraud scoring in `hesap-stats` (stolen cards, key and gift reselling, refund abuse) feeds SHIP.8's support tools. Peers: Steam and Epic checkout for time from cart to entitlement and recovery of failed payments. ## Verification and maintenance

Check this document with `python scripts/check-master-plan.py` from the repository root. It verifies the single
table, order, IDs, prerequisites, source routing and current documentation links; it does not test engine features.

Per slice: fulfill the linked contract, test the actual asset/runtime path, preserve last-good reload and record
quality/performance evidence. Local work uses changed modules plus blast radius, scoped CTest and incremental tidy;
whole-repository/configuration sweeps belong to CI. [BUILDING](BUILDING.md), [PRINCIPLES](PRINCIPLES.md) and
[SANITY](SANITY.md) remain binding. No performance claims without a saved full board in [bench](bench/README.md).

Update a row once with its evidence link; update a parent only when every child passes. Keep current focus as one
pointer in context. Sessions, ADRs, recipes, research and archives preserve knowledge; do not copy live Next lists
into them. A finding in the audit is assigned to a row here, not a new competing backlog. The user owns commits.
